messages:
anna: RFC follow-up on MHA layout — proposing a hybrid layout: per-head-contiguous for KV cache and per-sequence-contiguous for Q. TL;DR: should cut KV cache fragmentation and make appends cheap, at cost of occasional transpose when head_dim isn't aligned. Thoughts?

miguel: sounds promising. need numbers for small-batch long-seq cases. Ampere/Blackwell prefers contiguous head_dim for coalesced reads.

sophia: big +1 for KV cache append perf — per-head contiguous lets us append new K/V rows with a single memcpy. interleaved QKV causes strided writes which blow up latency on streaming workloads.

prateek: caveat: fused attention kernels expect NHWC-ish memory for fast vectorized matmul (batch, seq, head, hd). If we store NCHW-like we pay a remap cost before the fused kernel.

zhen: ran a quick bench — remap-to-fused layout costs ~8-12% for int8 kernels on short sequences (<64). For seq >= 512 remap amortizes and per-head cache wins 10-20% end-to-end.

runtime-bot: autotune heuristic proposal: if head_dim % 32 == 0 and seq_len >= 64 and caching_enabled -> prefer per_head_contiguous; else prefer per_seq_contiguous. fallback: strided kernel when remap overhead > threshold.

anna: we should microbenchmark two remap strategies: device memcpy of contiguous blocks vs a lightweight CUDA kernel that transposes & packs to 32B lanes. I'll add tests.

sophia: note on rotary/ALiBi: applying rotary per-head is simpler if the head dim is contiguous. For per-seq contiguous storage we need strided rotary ops or an extra gather. That impacts streaming latency.

prateek: prototype selector pseudocode:
```
# kernel selector (simplified)
if caching_enabled:
  if head_dim % 32 == 0 and seq_len >= 64 and batch <= 16:
    layout = 'per_head_contiguous'
  else:
    layout = 'per_seq_contiguous'
else:
  layout = 'per_seq_contiguous'
# pack stage: if quantized then pack_into_int8_aligned(layout)
```

zhen: another important bit: quantized inference (symm/affine int8) wants 32-byte alignment and packing order (row-major vs col-major) to match GEMM kernels. Add a pack-once stage after remap so subsequent requests reuse the packed buffer.

miguel: hybrid layout also complicates model-parallel sharding: shards expect contiguous QKV slices per GPU. we need to define a shard contract so the layout metadata can be interpreted by the sharder. otherwise cross-GPU collective dims get messy.

anna: agreed — propose we add a small layout metadata header to the model manifest: { layout: 'per_head'|'per_seq', head_dim, stride_info, packing } so sharders and runtime kernels know how to slice without guessing.

ci-bot: Added follow-up RFC document to /eng-runtime/rfcs and attached preliminary perf tables. link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/mha-layout-hybrid (internal)

prateek: :thumbsup: I'll spin up a prototype branch with the selector + a caching-aware transpose kernel and run across small/medium/large seq ranges.

anna: action items: prateek prototype kernel selector & transpose; zhen add int8 pack reuse pattern to benchmark; sophia add rotary microbench; miguel evaluate shard contract constraints. I'll collate numbers and update the RFC. Thanks everyone.
